review.label: squad/review
review.handoff: Explicit workflow_dispatch from a separate deterministic Actions-write-only job. GITHUB_TOKEN label events do not start labeled workflows; dispatch does. Workflow-level PR concurrency serializes automatic and human requests through comment publication, avoiding duplicate paid review sessions.
review.testPolicy: Full Research -> Plan -> Implement -> Review for static review preparation. Research inspects immutable source, Plan defines evidence checks, Implement produces only the static analysis evidence pack, and a distinct Squad Reviewer validates it. Each stage has its own domain artifact and serialized Scribe history/consumption. No source edits, PR checkout or PR code/tests/hooks/builds/installers. QA is not deployed; never invent dispatch or dynamic test success.

operatorNotes: Consumer configuration for the Grubify demo. Publication and repository settings are human-approved actions; workflow runs require the explicit repository-variable gate and authorized event provenance.

Publish only .gitignore, apm.yml, apm.lock.yaml, this config, BOTH .github/workflows/squad-watch.yml and .github/workflows/squad-review.yml, the no-AI .github/workflows/squad-apm-check.yml, and scripts/squad-watch/, plus the reviewed deletion of the inherited inverse SRE workflow. Do not publish generated agent assets, apm_modules, scratch files, CLI sessions or transcripts.

Before publication/activation: review all files and frozen dependencies, publish both workflows to main, verify squad/auto and squad/review, supply COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN as a dedicated fine-grained PAT with ONLY Copilot Requests and no repository permissions, and confirm model/CLI policies.

Keep default_workflow_permissions=read. Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests is required for built-in-token draft creation; neither workflow approves a PR. This GitHub setting combines creation and approval, so main protection and deterministic comment-only review remain necessary. A reviewed restricted GitHub App alternative requires a separate design.

Before activation, protect main with an active ruleset requiring PRs and appropriate human approvals/review, no bot/App bypass, no force pushes or deletions. Do not rely on read-by-default workflow permissions as branch protection.

The consumer removes inherited .github/workflows/sre-agent-investigate.yml issues.opened -> SRE. This demo goes SRE -> issue -> Squad, not the inverse direction; removing it avoids an unwanted second investigation/trigger loop and avoids requiring ARM_TOKEN/SRE_TRIGGER_URL in GitHub.

Only after prerequisites and explicit activation approval, set SQUAD_WATCH_ENABLED=true. Issues must be previewed/sanitized before publication, with no raw logs, identifiers, credentials, customer data or cloud resource identifiers.

An authorized write/maintain/admin collaborator applies squad/auto to an OPEN issue, or manually dispatches an OPEN issue number from main. Initial, request-producer and CURRENT rerun actors are independently checked before the interpretation secret, again after installation before model work, and before mutation. Issue author alone has no authority. Bots not resolved as write collaborators are denied.

Generation triggers remain issues.labeled/workflow_dispatch. Review is workflow_dispatch ONLY (automatic handoff or collaborator manual recovery), never pull_request/pull_request_target: this keeps the workflow definition itself on protected main, not a PR-proposed merge tree. Human-added squad/review is opt-in but must be followed by manual Squad Review dispatch with pr_number; merely adding that label does not schedule a review. Automatic review uses explicit dispatch, NOT the bot-generated label event. Both workflows must exist on protected main before activation.

Native --max-ai-credits is a SHARED parent/subagent SESSION SOFT CAP: minimum 30, default 90, dispatch range 30..90. A returning model response may overshoot; hidden compaction counts. It is NOT a token budget, premium-request count, estimated USD ceiling or HVE cost-ceiling. Timeout is an independent wall-clock bound.

Intended writes after activation: Git blobs/tree/commit, CREATE-ONLY squad/issue-N branch, one DRAFT PR closing N, exact squad/review label on that PR via Issues API, one explicit dispatch of the second Squad workflow, and one bounded evidence-labelled PR comment per PR/head. Fixed source-issue failure/no-change comments remain separate. Never approve, merge, mark ready, update branches/PR bodies, relabel the source issue or force-push. A label/dispatch failure leaves the created draft intact and fails visibly with its link; humans recover by verifying the draft/label then dispatching review, never regenerating/overwriting it.

Interpret has contents/issues/pull-requests READ only, persist-credentials=false and only the Copilot Requests secret at model runtime. Public APM dependencies use a read-only built-in token during installation. Apply independently validates the untrusted patch and never runs models, repository scripts, hooks, build tools or proposed code. CLI deny rules and secret-env-vars are defense in depth, NOT a sandbox or an exfiltration-proof guarantee.

Issue content is a JSON data file, not shell interpolation. Interpret and apply independently recheck issue hash/state/label, collaborators, exact main SHA and existing branch/PR. Apply repeats these checks immediately before writes. Stale, ambiguous, out-of-policy or missing-audit outputs fail closed.

Outputs: immutable request artifact, patch plus handoff manifest artifact, and sanitized event-scoped federation audit on the draft branch. Artifacts retain 1 day; committed audit persists. No raw CLI stdout/stderr, session/log files or environment dumps are uploaded or committed.

Only backend/frontend source and current event federation audit paths are accepted; no infrastructure, workflows, credentials, package-manager manifests at repo root, .git, binaries, symlinks, submodules, attributes, control filenames or other sub-squads. Human-owned single-squad promotion or disambiguated event names require a separately reviewed policy expansion.

Partial/full reruns use immutable producer artifact IDs and names retained in job outputs, never current-attempt guesses or cross-job runner paths. The request's runAttempt remains its prepare origin; handoff.requestRunAttempt and handoff.runAttempt identify request origin and interpretation producer separately. Apply may execute later, but neither origin may be in the future. Missing/expired artifacts fail closed and require a fresh approved run, not provenance rewriting.

Federation ownership and member trigger.ref/eventId are checked against the exact trusted Git base tree before model work and again against independently reconstructed base objects during handoff validation. Human ownership or mismatched provenance cannot be rewritten into watch ownership. New blank init and correctly provenanced owned/orphan member resume remain supported. Existing registry/routes and unrelated histories/rates remain byte-intact; same-member histories and decisions are append-only. Shared state preserves unrelated member lists, policy, notification, escalation and aggregate run values; only current-event membership/activity, turn and timestamp may change.

Risk Stop stops Implement; over-ceiling stops new children; cannot-confirm remains blocked. Findings go under Blocking findings in decisions.md and the DRAFT body. Impactful-Action gates never proceed.

Upstream fixes/adaptations: explicit CLI agent and version pin; frozen consumer APM installation instead of assuming maintainer assets; strict numeric open-issue/main dispatch validation; shared issue concurrency across label/dispatch; independent artifact/path/mode/secret/audit validation; create-only branch/PR idempotency; no credential in git remote URL; no execution of agent-modified New-ChangeFragment.ps1; reproduce blocking findings in PR body; remove release-specific fragments and incomplete optional review/escalation scopes.

IMPORTANT reproduced APM 0.29.0 limitation: --frozen accepted a changed v0.18.0 root reference in an isolated copy and rewrote its lock (315 to 52 dependencies). It is NOT by itself a reliable pin/integrity boundary. Consumer guards the exact approved LF-canonical manifest+lock digests before install, requires byte-identical manifests afterward, and runs apm audit --ci before any model invocation. Do not upgrade APM or bypass failures with --force/--no-policy.

Prior local validation: genuine isolated v0.18.1 frozen install completed 315 dependencies with byte-identical root manifest/lock; original checkout apm audit --ci passed all 10 checks. Official Linux release checksum and runner-image PowerShell 7 availability were verified. Follow-up local rerun/provenance and trusted-base federation fixes: 57 offline contract cases passed, including partial interpret/apply-only/full reruns, unauthorized current actors, wrong producer provenance, stale pre-model checks, human-ownership rewriting, mismatched member provenance, registry/routing/metadata tampering, blank init, owned/orphan resume and append-only histories. YAML/JSON, embedded JS/Bash, pinned Action SHA, permission and approved lock parsing checks also passed without new tool installs. Tests use disposable local clone/tree fixtures, not a real squad init. Offline checks do not prove live Actions rerun output retention/artifact downloads, GitHub permissions, entitlement, CLI role dispatch, AI output quality or Linux end-to-end execution. No actual AI run, publishing or remote mutation was performed; activation remains unset/inactive.

CLI agent identifier is the filename without .agent.md, not the optional display name; GitHub custom-agent configuration documentation distinguishes these. Explicit --agent squad-federation-coordinator is used. Live loading/dispatch requires the separately approved smoke test.

APM Copilot deployment flattens agent/instruction directories while some HVE narrative references retain nested squad paths. The trusted runtime spine explicitly directs basename resolution to installed .github/agents, .github/instructions and .agents/skills/squad instead of rewriting signed/locked third-party assets.
Fresh Watch events intentionally omit an explicit squad= argument: explicit targets must already be registered. Event-scoped initialization is driven by structural Watch provenance instead.
Offline fixture cleanup is confined to its disposable clone, restores the index and baseline files, and handles adversarial directory-shaped fixtures without hard-resetting the user's checkout.

Set SQUAD_WATCH_ENABLED=true in Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables as a REPOSITORY VARIABLE only after explicit approval. This gate protects BOTH generation and review; with it unset/false no model or mutation job runs. Store COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN separately as an Actions SECRET. Create/verify both squad/auto and squad/review labels before activation.

Two genuine independent coordinator sessions consume TWO native shared-session soft allowances: generation and review both default to the configured maximum of 90. Callers may explicitly lower generation to 30..90 for non-demo work. Neither allowance is a guaranteed hard bound, USD ceiling or promise of a successful full run.

Review installs only approved main APM assets, reads bounded API snapshots of exact PR base/head as UNTRUSTED JSON, and initializes event member pr-N through real Watch bootstrap (no explicit squad= on fresh events). It routes installed tester primary Squad Reviewer and appropriate Code Review Functional/Standards alternates with real domain artifacts/per-role histories; QA is not deployed in this locked cast and must not be invented. Static review only: no untrusted code or test execution and no dynamic-pass claims.

Automatic handoff validates source workflow path/repository/main SHA/run/attempt, successful apply job, artifact ID/name/digest, generation actors and actual draft PR parent/head/base/label. Human review requests require initial/current collaborators and same-repo open main-target PRs. Each phase rechecks current main, PR head/base/label and authorization. Review comment markers are deterministic per PR/head; shared concurrency and pre-model/pre-publish duplicate checks prevent replay. Changed heads/labels fail closed; no silent stale comment.

Review audit/report artifacts are sanitized and bounded, retain one day, contain event pr-N state/roster/decisions/consumption/domain evidence/history (not raw CLI transcripts), and are never committed onto the source branch. The public PR comment distinguishes model-authored static findings from verified dispatch artifact presence and explicitly says tests were not executed. Heuristic secret/private-ID rejection is defense in depth, not an exfiltration-proof sandbox.

Latest local second-Squad validation: 58 generation contracts plus 63 independent-review contracts (121 total), including the actual embedded dispatch code, source-versus-review run IDs, source attempt/artifact metadata/digest and successful apply producer, actual draft/head/parent linkage, collaborator/fork/stale/duplicate rejection, partial rerun provenance, escaped output/domain evidence/caps, label and dispatch failure recovery, and no-change zero writes. YAML/JSON, embedded JS/Bash syntax, pinned action equivalence, permission scopes and exact approved APM manifest/315-dependency lock hashes also checked offline. Disposable fixtures were removed; no real squad state, secret access, AI charge, commit, publication or remote mutation. Live Actions/API permissions, artifact retention/downloads, Linux execution, CLI model entitlement and genuine HVE role dispatch remain unverified and need separately approved validation.

Automatic review is scheduled immediately after successful generation apply/result upload by its separate Actions-write-only dispatch job. No additional PAT permissions are needed; apply's Issues-write is solely for the required PR label (in addition to its existing validation/branch/PR operations). Second-Squad publication has Issues-write for one PR issue-comment, with no contents/PR/Actions write or model/secret. A final head/label/actor recheck precedes publication; GitHub has no atomic head-conditional comment API, so the comment names the exact reviewed base/head and never claims current-head approval.

If generation is rerun after a draft/branch already exists, preparation explicitly skips rather than creating new result artifacts or duplicate work. Expired/missing/old-attempt linkage and main/head changes fail closed. Humans verify the existing draft and label, then dispatch Squad Review on current main with only pr_number for recovery. Repeating review on an already-commented exact head skips model work; a new authorized head requires a new request.

APM package integrity hashes raw file paths and bytes, NOT the LF-canonical root manifest/lock text. The previous Windows-generated package hashes captured Git core.autocrlf=true CRLF checkouts and failed on Linux. Re-materialize approved immutable commits in a CLEAN Linux checkout using APM 0.29.0; compare the ENTIRE graph and deployed-file witnesses before reviewing any new hashes and updating approvedLockLfSha256. Never normalize downloaded packages or substitute a reported actual hash to silence a failure; legitimate upstream CRLF and binary bytes must stay intact.

Both model workflows use install-apm.cjs through the shared installer. The helper scopes Git core.autocrlf=false/core.eol=lf to APM children with apm.gitconfig, bypasses ambient global/system checkout defaults and credential helpers, preserves frozen/raw-hash validation, checks byte-identical root inputs and runs audit --ci. Public acquisition may use the existing read-only built-in token; no global Git configuration is changed. The path-filtered Squad APM Linux integrity workflow exercises the actual installer on PR/push with contents:read, no secrets, no model and no application execution.

Windows recovery: use a NEW disposable checkout in WSL Ubuntu's Linux filesystem with git -c core.autocrlf=false clone, copy only the reviewed manifest/lock/config/scripts, set process-local APM_CACHE_DIR to a NEW owned directory in that checkout, and run node scripts/squad-watch/install-apm.cjs <absolute-path-to-approved-Linux-APM-0.29.0-executable>. The helper also scopes native Windows Git defaults, but APM 0.29.0 can still hit Windows path-length limits in deeply nested checkouts/caches; use WSL rather than changing system settings. Do not reuse an old CRLF apm_modules/cache, delete the user's cache, run --force/--no-policy, or regenerate/approve a lock merely to make it pass. Keep existing generated assets untouched; any cache mismatch fails closed and requires a separate clean checkout/cache. Offline coverage: node scripts/squad-watch/test-apm.cjs; Linux release checksum and full installer remain separate real-install checks.

2026-10-15 local portability validation: changed exactly 80 hve-core skill package hashes, retaining every other lock field and all 315 commit anchors. Verified regenerated payloads against pinned Git blob IDs, preserving six legitimate upstream CRLF files. The checksum-verified Linux APM 0.29.0 full shared installer passed in a fresh isolated WSL-native checkout with byte-identical manifest/lock, all 10 audit checks, all 1795 deployed paths and all 27 Squad cast agents; CLI 1.0.93 was checked by version only. A second frozen pass left inputs unchanged, real audit denied an isolated deployed-skill tamper, and restored audit passed. Offline suites passed 58 generation + 64 review + 21 portability contracts; portability contracts passed on Windows and Linux. This supersedes earlier unverified Linux APM-install statements, not live Actions/model/entitlement/role-dispatch validation. No actual AI invocation, repository commit, publication, remote mutation or settings change was performed.

Handoff recovery: ordinary Squad state may be Git-ignored. Both stage helpers explicitly collect only exact shared audit files plus the current event member, validate scope, regular files, parents and bounds before force-adding those explicit paths, then retain all independent ownership/provenance/append-only checks. Other ignored members and runtime trees are never force-added. Missing bootstrap evidence, including a zero-output coordinator, fails closed rather than counting as a successful no-change run. The validator never creates Squad state; real Scribe evidence remains mandatory.

Safe runtime-status.json diagnostics are retained for one day and summarized even after coordinator/stage failure. Only allowlisted step outcomes, exit code, termination category, fixed audit/role-history presence, fixed four-stage journal availability/status, native completed-prefix cast/Scribe counts, bounded root-hook statistics and bounded typed failure/accounting projections are emitted. No raw parser errors, artifact filenames, call/session IDs, CLI output, issue/model text, environment or token is uploaded. Presence and failed-run counts are not usable dispatch proof; exit zero does not establish completion.

2026-10-19 local RPI correction supersedes earlier single-role evidence claims: BOTH event sessions require Research, Plan, Implement, Review using the installed primary charters, plus bootstrap and one fully serialized Scribe handoff per stage. Scribe writes pipeline.json and stage-specific append-only history/consumption; every stage has a separate substantive event-scoped domain artifact. A genuine blocked prefix is not completion, and cannot authorize application changes before Implement. A blocked PR review never publishes a completed review report.

The ephemeral runtime adapter validates required RPI charters/skills, retains the full deployed cast, maps deployed agent dependencies to qualified CLI identifiers and VS Code model display names to CLI model IDs, and registers all installed skills. Frozen APM assets and lock hashes are not edited. Only unresolved optional agent allowlist entries are omitted; a required missing role or skill fails bootstrap.

CLI 1.0.98 uses a new isolated private session under runner.temp and an explicit session UUID. A trusted copied collector reduces its native subagent.started/completed events to allowlisted role names and ordinal start/end positions bound to the immutable request and producing attempt. No raw session, tool arguments/results, reasoning or prose is uploaded. Missing, unsupported, cancelled, failed or overlapping Scribe events fail closed; no artifact-only fallback is allowed. Handoff/apply and review/stage/publication independently validate ordered role dispatch and serialized Scribe barriers. Runtime lifecycle proves dispatch, not correctness, authorship attestation or a sandbox.

2026-10-19 run 39324042639 after PR #19: coordinator exit zero and native collection succeeded, but deterministic stage rejected Missing per-role dispatch history. Six broad disk/index presence flags do not establish which children ran or why history was absent; the retained evidence cannot prove a particular model cause. Earlier PR #12 success was not a full-four-role RPI proof.

Local bootstrap/stop repair separates initialization from final completed-stage evidence in both prompts. Blank federation and member initialization are separate single-type, single-root Scribe payloads; member initialization creates only its own Scribe orchestration history, never future role history. Every actual stage then gets serialized history/consumption and artifact readback before the next stage. Final member inner-run summaries use the member schema, not the federation meta-run template.

Runtime plugin intentionally uses the CLI legacy manifest (no Agent Plugins $schema) with hooks: hooks/hooks.json. Pinned CLI 1.0.98 native hook discovery and command execution were exercised offline: exactly one enabled root agentStop, zero hook parse warnings/errors, PLUGIN_ROOT substituted into the command environment; a synthetic bootstrap-only stop returned block plus the Research instruction through the actual native command processor. This did not invoke inference or test the model's response. Agent Plugins schemas instead require com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json; the formats must not be mixed. Plugin command cwd defaults to the plugin root, so launchers export a fixed trusted checkout root and bind private context before inference.

The trusted copied root agentStop command reads only request-hash-bound fixed session events and bounded event audit evidence. It requests the actual next missing stage, or Scribe history/readback rather than rerunning an observed completed role. Genuine blocked prefixes may stop; Risk Stop/cannot-confirm/over-ceiling are never overridden. It writes only its bounded statistics in runner.temp, never domain/state/history/Git. It has at most eight blocks and stops after three unchanged reentries. Hook crashes/timeouts/unsupported input or credit exhaustion may fail open at the CLI, but unchanged deterministic stage/apply/publication gates still reject incomplete evidence. There is one CLI per launcher, the same default maximum 90 shared credits and 30-minute timeout; no automatic workflow retry or new paid session.

These repairs are local until human-reviewed publication to main. No new live AI session, workflow dispatch, commit, push, review comment, cloud action or settings mutation was authorized. Offline synthetic lifecycle and real native hook-registration checks do not establish live end-to-end lifecycle compatibility, model entitlement, Scribe authorship or successful full-role execution within 90 credits/30 minutes; an approved fresh-event Linux run is still required. Existing draft branches are never overwritten; review recovery remains manual workflow_dispatch for an eligible PR/head.

2026-10-20 generation run 39385384526 on the merged bootstrap repair exited 1, with handoff skipped. Safe retained evidence reports two completed native Scribes, no four-stage role completions or member audit, and two root-hook checks/blocks continuing member-init. The hook therefore ran; this differs from the older zero-exit missing-role-history handoff. The exact CLI failure cause is unproven: raw native events were not retained from the expired runner. Neither allowance exhaustion nor auth, quota, model or tool failure can responsibly be inferred.

Local diagnostic repair keeps reading the bounded private native stream after terminal/error, parse or lifecycle failure, retaining only the completed valid prefix and allowlisted later facts. Native errors, aborts, cancellation, invalid lifecycle or malformed event streams still deny native proof and final collection; no failed run becomes successful. Accounting anomalies are diagnostic warnings only: they degrade reported cost coverage, never block otherwise valid RPI dispatch/history or trigger another role. Both workflows already report diagnostics after nonzero exit without final collection. Diagnostic context is explicitly bound or unavailable; configured shared cap is read only from the immutable bound request. The model, prompts, roster, 90-credit maximum, 30-minute timeout, permissions and one-session launch policy are unchanged.

Typed error categories are quota, rate_limit, authentication, authorization, policy, context_limit, query or other; codes are exact category-specific documented allowlists, with unknown strings normalized and status restricted to integer 0..999. Upstream CAPI session_quota_exceeded is NOT evidence of local shared --max-ai-credits exhaustion; account/organization scope is unknown. Abort autopilot_credit_limit identifies an objective cap, not the shared session cap. Optional session_limits_exhausted.requested is ephemeral and usually absent; absence proves nothing. Typed observations and shutdown routine/error metadata are not a proven explanation for the CLI exit; exitCause stays unknown. Messages, stacks, URLs, provider parameters, errorReason and identifiers never enter safe output.

Accounting uses only root-scoped durable session.usage_checkpoint/session.shutdown totalNanoAiu snapshots: 1e9 nanoAIU is one AI credit, not premium requests, tokens or dollars. Pinned 1.0.98 durable event schemas place optional aiCreditsStatus inside internal accountingSnapshot, not directly on those event data objects. Missing status/amount remains unavailable/null as applicable; explicit zero with partial/unavailable coverage is not a free-run claim. Only the last valid nonregressing cumulative snapshot is retained, never summed with earlier snapshots, per-call receipts or per-agent/model metrics. Child snapshots are ignored and counted; malformed/regressing accounting is flagged and coverage becomes unavailable. Complete status covers reported observed calls, not an independently measured bill or assurance that the final snapshot covered the entire run.

For the next separately approved fresh run, inspect only safe runtime-status.json typed category/code, abort/shutdown scope, context binding, accounting source/status/coverage, exit and hook facts. If those stable fields do not identify a cause, it remains unknown; investigate any native output privately under an explicitly reviewed retention/access policy rather than publishing transcripts or adding message-regex guesses. This change neither reruns a workflow nor claims the underlying live CLI cause was fixed.
